children: A federal judge on Wednesday barred the Federal Communications Commission from launching an early review of ABC’s broadcast licenses, ruling in favor of the network’s argument that the Trump administration was infringing on its free speech rights.

U.S. District Judge Loren AliKhan in Washington, D.C., granted ABC’s request for a temporary restraining order and a preliminary injunction on First Amendment grounds. The network accuses the FCC of violating its free speech rights in retaliation against programming decisions that the Trump administration dislikes.
AliKhan noted in her ruling that the network was likely to succeed on its First Amendment claim. “This is not a close case,” she wrote.

AliKhan, who was nominated by former President Joe Biden, said ABC had detailed “a campaign of retaliation against them in response to their exercise of their First Amendment rights,” which on its own is an ‘irreparable injury.’”
ABC and its parent company, Disney

, sued the FCC and FCC Commissioner Brendan Carr in August, several months after the commission ordered eight ABC-owned stations to submit renewal applications for their broadcast licenses years ahead of schedule.
“Today’s decision is an important victory for the First Amendment,” a spokesperson for ABC News said in a statement.

An FCC spokesperson said in a statement that the part of the decision granting ABC’s motion “is wrong on the facts and wrong on the law,” adding that the agency “looks forward to prevailing in full on this matter.”

The case is one of several legal skirmishes between President Donald Trump’s administration and news outlets — including The Associated Press — over their coverage and access to the executive branch since the Republican returned to the White House nearly two years ago.

title: Court blocks FCC move on ABC licenses in free speech ruling for Disney
